_provenance: Signals REBUILT this session from the current verified evidence base - the 6 real consumer-taxonomy themes (re-evaluated for research convergence against the new 10-paper peer-reviewed corpus, not merely carried over) plus 4 new signals that emerge purely from the research corpus and have no consumer-taxonomy analogue. Signals are not padded to a target count - if a signal has one independent source family, it is reported as SINGLE_SOURCE_FAMILY, not upgraded for symmetry. CONTESTED is used once, where two real studies genuinely disagree (see health_outcome_uncertainty).

signals.name: Filtration-to-health-benefit evidence is genuinely split
signals.meaning: One real RCT (RP-08) found a significant asthma-control benefit from HEPA filtration; two other real studies (RP-03, RP-05) measuring related pollutants/symptoms found no such association.
signals.direction: Contested - do not treat as resolved in either direction
signals.limitations: RP-08 is a single-center trial in a niche journal, needs independent replication; RP-03/RP-05 measured different specific outcomes (ammonia; self-reported symptoms), so this is not a strict head-to-head contradiction.
signals.contradictions: RP-08 (positive clinical result) vs. RP-03 and RP-05 (no measured symptom benefit) - see research_tensions.json tension T6.
signals.design_consequence: Never assert a health-outcome claim from PM-reduction evidence alone; a verified-clean/verified-performance claim is more defensible until RP-08 is independently replicated.

research_support.title: Indoor environmental health and asthma relief
research_support.found: +2.2 ACT points, +27.7% symptom-free days vs. placebo (p<=0.004).

research_support.title: Effectiveness of portable HEPA air cleaners... children with asthma
research_support.found: PM2.5 reduced 60% but no symptom/clinical outcome reported in this result.

research_support.title: Self-reported health impacts of DIY air cleaner use
research_support.found: No association observed between usage and self-reported symptoms.

research_support.found: No association was found between DIY air-cleaner usage and self-reported symptoms; usage itself was low, and loud operating noise was cited as a barrier to use.

research_support.title: Reduction of personal PM2.5 exposure via indoor air filtration systems in Detroit: an intervention study
research_support.found: True-HEPA cut personal PM2.5 exposure 53% and indoor concentration 60%; a cheaper HEPA-type filter still cut exposure 31% and concentration 52%.

research_support.found: Raw averages misleadingly showed higher PM in the active-filtration group (higher source strength homes); background-period PM was ~36% lower with active filtration, and loss rates rose ~15-130% with fan speed.

signals.name: Sensor precision != sensor accuracy
signals.meaning: Consumer-grade IAQ sensors can track relative change well while reporting materially wrong absolute numbers - a 'smart' claim needs a trust qualifier, not just a reading.
signals.direction: Constraint on autonomy claims - more sensors is not automatically more intelligence
signals.limitations: Both studies test PM2.5/CO2 sensors specifically; may not generalize to other pollutant sensors (e.g. VOC).
signals.contradictions: None identified - both studies agree sensor accuracy is context-dependent.
signals.design_consequence: Any autonomous/reactive control claim should disclose the conditions under which its sensor reading is and isn't trustworthy.

research_support.title: Low-cost sensors for indoor air quality monitoring: A systematic review
research_support.found: Performance varies significantly with humidity, temperature, pollutant source; most devices lack formal validation.

research_support.title: Validating the performance of low-cost IAQ sensors through co-location
research_support.found: A sensor can be precise (good relative trend) while inaccurate (biased absolute value) at the same time.

signals.name: Constant vs. auto is a real trade, not a solved problem
signals.meaning: Constant operation filters measurably more (66% vs 40% PM2.5 reduction) than threshold-triggered auto mode, but auto mode cuts runtime, noise, and energy substantially.
signals.direction: Design constraint - no single default operating mode is strictly better
signals.limitations: Single trial, Toronto multifamily buildings only, one-week arms per condition.
signals.contradictions: None - single-source finding, treat as directional not definitive.
signals.design_consequence: Ship the constant/auto choice as a visible, explainable trade-off, not a hidden factory default.

research_support.title: The impact of portable air cleaners on indoor PM concentrations and perceptions of IAQ
research_support.found: Constant mode: 66% PM2.5 reduction. Auto mode: 40% reduction with sharply less runtime.

signals.name: The floor is a source, not just a sink
signals.meaning: Ordinary walking measurably resuspends floor-deposited particles back into room air - a real spatial dynamic the standard stationary-room-purifier model does not directly address.
signals.direction: Opens a design question - does NOT establish a floor-level purifier would outperform a room-level one
signals.limitations: Single controlled lab chamber, one carpet/dust load, no home field data, no purifier tested at all in this study.
signals.contradictions: None - single-source finding; the 'floor purifier would be better' inference is explicitly NOT supported and must not be asserted.
signals.design_consequence: Spatial-source modeling for sizing/placement should not assume deposited particles stay deposited - but no placement claim follows from this evidence alone.

research_support.title: PM10, PM2.5, PM1, and PM0.1 resuspension due to human walking
research_support.found: 10 minutes of walking measurably raised PM concentrations across all four size fractions.
